source_proof_observations: Chapter 31 gives elliptic regularity alternatives: C^{1,1} domains with Lipschitz principal coefficients, convex domains, and polygonal corner regularity. It explicitly does not support a universal H^2 conclusion on arbitrary Lipschitz/polyhedral domains.
Chapter 32 derives conforming Poisson FEM estimates through Céa, a quasi-interpolant, and an Aubin–Nitsche dual problem; its L2 rate depends on a stated regularity pickup s, and h^{r+1} needs s=1.
Chapter 33 gives nonzero Dirichlet lifting and explicit quadrature consistency/stability conditions; the quadrature estimates are not unconditional.

bounded_section.reading_status: Bounded complete reading of §49.4.2, Babuška–Brezzi theorem and proof (PDF pp. 12–15 of 16); other chapter pages were not fully read and are not used as proof evidence.

source_proof_observations: Chapters 8, 11, and 12 provide matching affine mesh conventions, shape-regularity, local Bramble–Hilbert interpolation and inverse/trace estimates. Lagrange point-value interpolation has extra Sobolev embedding assumptions; quasi-interpolation/projection handles weaker regularity.

Chapters 24–27 derive weak formulations and the abstract Lax–Milgram/BNB, Fortin, Céa, Petrov–Galerkin, and Strang arguments. Variational crimes require a stable discrete form and a consistency defect bound.

Chapters 36–38 analyze Crouzeix–Raviart, Nitsche, and symmetric interior penalty methods with explicit broken norms, consistency, coercivity thresholds, and duality assumptions. L2 rates require elliptic pickup s>1/2 for the displayed nonconforming estimates.

Chapters 46–48 develop compact-operator eigenapproximation. The conforming symmetric theory gives one-sided upper eigenvalue bounds and best-approximation-squared errors; the compact nonsymmetric theory requires operator-norm convergence and primal/adjoint regularity on generalized eigenspaces.
Chapter 49 §49.4.2 proves the reflexive-space Babuška–Brezzi conditions: kernel inf-sup plus adjoint kernel condition and a separate uniform constraint inf-sup.

Chapter 50 separates discrete stability from continuous stability, proves mixed error bounds using a Fortin map and discrete kernel, and analyzes Schur-complement, augmented-Lagrangian, Uzawa, and block Krylov methods.

Chapters 53–55 prove the Stokes weak problem and discrete error estimates under a divergence inf-sup condition; they identify stable/unstable pairs, macroelement hypotheses, Fortin arguments, and the special divergence-preserving roles of bubbles and discontinuous pressures.

unread_parts: Chapters 1–8 and 10; front matter and bibliography except for citation orientation.
source_proof_observations: Chapter 9 states Brezzi splitting, discrete LBB stability, Fortin criterion, and mixed Céa estimates; its RT construction gives commuting divergence projection and H(div)-conforming normal traces.
Chapter 11 states the Gelfand triple time-continuity theorem and gives the parabolic BNB existence proof under measurable, uniformly bounded and coercive time-dependent forms.

Chapter 12 defines cG(r) and dG(r) time-space spaces, proves dG stability by interval test functions and jumps, and states temporal/spatial a priori error estimates under smoothness and adjoint regularity assumptions.

complete_relevant_sections.section: §7.3 Spectral approximation of the Stokes equations and §7.4 Spectral-projection method for Navier–Stokes equations

unread_parts: All of Chapters 1 except §1.8; Chapters 4–6; Chapters 7 other than §§7.3–7.4; all other unlisted sections and appendices.
source_proof_observations: Chapter 1 §1.8 proves weighted Jacobi projection rates in Sobolev norms; its Gauss–Lobatto interpolation estimate is quoted with proof referred elsewhere, while the Chebyshev analytic-function exponential bound is derived in the notes.

Chapter 2 derives polynomial and Fourier differentiation matrices, Chebyshev BVP collocation with general boundary conditions, and weak-form/finite-element preconditioning. It reports N^4 spectral-radius and condition-number growth for Chebyshev second-derivative collocation; these are operator conditioning facts, not PDE convergence guarantees.

Chapter 3 develops compact Legendre/Chebyshev Galerkin bases, quadrature, preconditioning, higher-order/Petrov–Galerkin methods, and weighted spectral error estimates. For some zero-order-free cases the L2 rate uses a duality argument; several technical interpolation results are cited rather than proved.

Chapter 7 §7.3 makes the Stokes pressure-space choice explicitly inf-sup dependent and derives error estimates carrying β_N. Section 7.4 describes projection schemes for unsteady Navier–Stokes; its author states that a rigorous proof of the advertised second-order estimate for one consistent splitting scheme was unavailable in that source. This dated remark is recorded as a source-limited proof gap, not as a current recognized open problem.

source_proof_observations: The continuous heat problem is posed in the evolution triple H^1_0 ↪ L^2 ↪ H^{-1}; the notes state well-posedness by reference rather than proving it.
The energy estimates test by u and u_t. Semi-discrete FEM uses the Ritz projection, giving the exact error equation L_h(u_h−R_hu)=Q_h(I−R_h)u_t and stability estimates.

Duality, semigroup smoothing, initial-data approximation, and spatial regularity produce conditional L2 and superconvergence rates; fully discrete Euler/CN and time-Galerkin estimates require separate time regularity.

Adaptivity I: Design and Convergence of AFEM
Adaptivity II: General Operators and Extensions

unread_parts: Lecture 5 and later chapters (printed pp. 48 onward).
source_proof_observations: Lecture 1 proves energy Céa and residual/error equivalence for a bounded coercive variational form and gives Clément interpolation rates.

Lecture 2 gives residual reliability, local efficiency up to data oscillation, Dörfler bulk marking, interior-node refinement, oscillation reduction, and linear AFEM convergence for the symmetric model problem.

Lecture 3 proves quasi-orthogonality and a combined error/oscillation contraction for a nonsymmetric convection form only under a sufficiently small initial mesh relative to convection; for zero convection it removes that restriction.

Lecture 4 derives optimal complexity first for the Laplacian, piecewise-constant forcing, P1 elements and an approximation class; the more general coefficient-dependent result is stated with proof referred to another paper. This is not used as a locally proved universal AFEM theorem.

source_proof_observations: The note presents a periodic vorticity/stream-function Fourier pseudospectral method for 2D incompressible Navier–Stokes, semi-implicit time stepping, physical-space nonlinear products and the 2/3 de-aliasing truncation rule. source_proof_observations: The official problem statement defines alternatives A/B (global smooth solutions on R^3 / periodic torus for all smooth decaying or periodic initial data with zero force) and C/D (a smooth forced breakdown example on the corresponding domain). It separately summarizes established 2D global smoothness, 3D small-data global and arbitrary-data local smoothness, Leray weak existence, and CKN partial regularity.
The current official status page retrieved 2026-10-12 states “Active.”

The 11 September 2026 announcement says CMI is sharing excitement surrounding an announcement that the problem has apparently been settled and says “The process is deliberately unhurried, but we will provide updates.” It gives no proof artifact or details identifying a submitter or which of alternatives A–D is claimed. The page status and announcement claim are recorded separately; the claim is pending verification.
